item.title: 🎧 LISTEN #1 — The SaaS Podcast: Founder-Led Sales to $1M ARR With Just 10 Customers
item.content:encoded:
Score: 76/100 | Listen Fully | Confidence: low

Originally published 10 Sep 2026

High relevance to eCommerce and product strategy. Features Felix Hoffmann (ex-Zalando pricing lead) sharing concrete tactical frameworks for data cold-starts, algorithm risk mitigation, and SaaS pricing.

Summary

Felix Hoffmann, founder of 7Learnings and former price optimization lead at Zalando, details how he built a predictive pricing SaaS for large retailers from zero to $1M ARR with only 10 customers. He covers solving the initial data cold-start problem by selling a paid consulting project to acquire retailer transaction data, structuring risk-reducing A/B test pilots for conservative retail buyers, navigating early algorithmic failures, and choosing fixed SaaS pricing over gain-share models.

Key Ideas

  • 7Learnings solved the enterprise AI data cold start by selling a paid consulting project to a major retailer and retaining rights to train its predictive pricing models on the transaction dataset.
  • To overcome enterprise retail buyer aversion to automated pricing, early pilots were structured as 50/50 product assortment A/B tests where the algorithm managed half the portfolio alongside human merchandisers.
  • 7Learnings intentionally rejected gain-share or success-based pricing despite proven uplift, choosing predictable fixed SaaS pricing to eliminate customer disputes over baseline sales attribution.

Implications

['Product managers building B2B AI products can overcome data bootstrap issues by packaging initial custom services that grant data licensing rights.', 'Enterprise risk can be de-risked by designing products to support side-by-side A/B deployment directly against existing legacy/manual workflows.']
